summary.title: Synthesis, Biological Activity and Molecular Docking of New Tricyclic Series as αglucosidase Inhibitors
summary.authors: Hatem A Abuelizz; Azman N I Nor; Iwana; Rohaya Ahmad; Anouar El-Hassane; Mohamed Marzouk; Rashad Al-Salahi
summary.executive_summary: Diabetes mellitus is a global health crisis, with prevalence rising from 4.7% in 1980 to 8.5% in 2014, largely driven by Type II diabetes characterized by ineffective insulin action. Current management strategies often rely on α-glucosidase inhibitors like acarbose to delay carbohydrate hydrolysis and reduce postprandial glucose levels. However, existing agents suffer from significant gastrointestinal side effects, such as flatulence and diarrhea, which reduce patient compliance. To address this, the authors synthesized 25 new tricyclic hybrids based on a pyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-one scaffold, a structure previously noted for fungicidal activity. These compounds were evaluated for their ability to inhibit α-glucosidase, an enzyme that interferes with digestive enzymes to decrease glucose absorption. The study identified two standout compounds, 6h and 6d, which demonstrated superior inhibitory activity compared to the reference drug acarbose. Specifically, compound 6h exhibited the highest inhibition with an IC50 of 104.07 mM. Molecular docking studies were conducted to understand the binding mechanisms, revealing that compound 6h forms a stable ligand-α-glucosidase complex. This stability is attributed to extra hydrogen bond interactions and specific directional binding guided by the Trp329 residue within the enzyme's active site. The research provides a new structural insight for developing clinically effective antidiabetic drugs that differ from commonly employed carbasugars, potentially offering a solution to the side effect profile of current treatments.

claims.description: Compound 6h is the most potent inhibitor among the synthesized series.
Trp329 is a critical residue for the binding conformation of the inhibitors.

Molecular docking studies were conducted to understand the binding mechanisms, revealing that compound 6h forms a stable ligand-α-glucosidase complex. This stability is attributed to extra hydrogen bond interactions and specific directional binding guided by the Trp329 residue within the enzyme's active site. The research provides a new structural insight for developing clinically effective antidiabetic drugs that differ from commonly employed carbasugars, potentially offering a solution to the side effect profile of current treatments.

Research Context
Diabetes prevalence has increased globally from 108 million in 1980 to 422 million. Type II diabetes results from ineffective action of insulin. Current α-glucosidase inhibitors like acarbose cause gastrointestinal side effects. These side effects are the major cause for reduced patient compliance. Sugar mimetic agents require tedious synthesis and have limitations. Pyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5,-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones are effective fungicidal agents.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to develop new α-glucosidase inhibitors to overcome side effects. Modifying accepted scaffolds like pyridine and triazole may yield active compounds. New compounds should exhibit IC 50 values lower than that of acarbose. Molecular docking will reveal insights into the binding mode of new leads. The valienamine moiety in acarbose mimics the oxocarbenium ion-like transition state. A significant inhibitory activity was observed for the newly synthesized compounds.

Methodological Details
Twenty-five tricyclic 2-phenoxypyrido[3,2e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones were synthesized. The enzyme was treated with equal concentrations (100 µg/mL) of each compound. The test was repeated three times for each compound to obtain average percent inhibition. Eight compounds exhibiting more than 50% inhibition were further evaluated for IC 50. Compounds 3, 6c and 6d showed average percent inhibition of more than 60%. Acarbose was used as positive control prepared at a concentration of 200 µg/ml. Phosphate-buffered saline pH 6.5 was prepared at 20 °C using specific salts. The α-glucosidase enzyme solution was prepared from Baker's yeast type 1. Absorbance was measured at 405 nm after a 30 min incubation at 37 °C. Molecular docking used the Autodock software package with PDB code 3W37.

Procedures And Architectures
Starting material A was prepared according to a reported procedure. 1,2,4-triazole intermediate B was obtained by reacting with A in a basic medium. Reaction of compound 1 with alkyl or heteroalkyl halides gave expected products. Boiling equimolar amounts of target 1 and phosphorous pentasulfide furnished thione 3. Conversion of 3 into 4 was carried out in basic medium using benzyl bromide. Transformation of 1 into 5 employed phosphorous oxychloride as chlorinating agent. Reaction of 5 with hydroxylamine HCl provided the corresponding product 6e. Treatment of target 5 with several aromatic amines afforded compounds 6a-d. Chlorine was replaced in 5 by isoniazid in boiling toluene to give amidrazone 6i. Hydrazinolysis of 5 in boiling ethanol produced the corresponding compound 6f. Treatment of 6f with equimolar amounts of aldehydes resulted in hydrazone derivatives 6g and 6h. The original docked protein was downloaded from the RCSB data bank web site.

Key Results
Compounds 6h and 6d have shown stronger activity than that of acarbose. Compound 6h exhibited the highest inhibition with an IC 50 of 104.07 mM. The inhibitory activity of all the tested compounds was between 30% and 63%. Compounds 2a and 2d had average percent inhibitions of 50.36% and 57.48%, respectively. The IC 50 of compound 3 was 167.82 µM. The IC 50 of compound 2a was 304.13 µM. The IC 50 of compound 2d was 173.83 µM. The binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol). Acarbose can establish 10 hydrogen bonds with specific residues. Compound 6h can establish hydrogen bonds with Ala234, Arg552 and Asp469. Trp329 can also form hydrophobic bonds with compounds 2a and 6h.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Maximal inhibition activity of compound 6h is mainly attributable to its binding energy. Three hydrogen bonds enhance the ligand-α-glucosidase complex stability. Trp329 plays a significant role in directing the ligand in the binding site. The study provides a new structural insight for the development of novel inhibitors. New compounds differ from the commonly employed carbasugars. The number of established intermolecular hydrogen bonds is responsible for activity.

Contradictions And Limitations
Only two N-alkylated derivatives showed more than 50% average percent inhibition. Derivatives did not exhibit any inhibitory activity except for compounds 2a and 2d. This suggests that the derivatization site has no significant effect on activity.

Claims
Compound 6h is the most potent inhibitor among the synthesized series. Compound 6h exhibited the highest inhibition with an IC 50 of 104.07 mM. The binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol).  This study provides a new structural insight for the development of novel inhibitors.
Trp329 is a critical residue for the binding conformation of the inhibitors. Trp329 can also form hydrophobic bonds with compounds 2a and 6h. Trp329 plays a significant role in directing the ligand in the binding site.  Understanding this interaction aids in designing new clinically effective antidiabetic drugs.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The test was repeated three times for each compound to obtain average percent inhibition. The relative standard deviation of the binding energy was less than 2.34 kcal/mol.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the synthesis of 25 tricyclic hybrids with superior activity. 2. The strongest evidence is the IC 50 of 104.07 mM for compound 6h. 3. The future path involves transforming these leads into new clinical drugs.
